books.section: Topic 1.4 Columbian Exchange, Spanish Exploration, and Conquest
The Columbian Exchange Transforms the Americas
The Early Colonial Era: Spain Colonizes the New World

primary_sources: Nahua account of smallpox, Florentine Codex (16th century), compiled by Bernardino de Sahagun with Nahua scholars

parts.modelAnswer: The account describes the sick lying in their houses, unable to move or stir. So many fell ill at once that the healthy could not bury the dead.
parts.prompt: Identify one feature of the epidemic described in the account.

scoring.criterion: Earns the point for naming one accurate feature from the account, such as the sick unable to move, the unburied dead, or whole neighborhoods falling ill at once.
scoring.notEarned: Naming a feature not in the account, such as Spanish soldiers spreading the disease on purpose, does not earn the point.

parts.modelAnswer: The epidemic emptied towns and broke the systems that fed and defended them. With so many dead or too sick to fight, Spanish forces faced far less resistance than an untouched empire would have offered.
parts.prompt: Explain how the epidemic described in the account helped Spanish conquest.

scoring.criterion: Earns the point for explaining how the epidemic aided conquest, such as by emptying towns, breaking food systems, or leaving too few fighters to resist.
scoring.notEarned: Stating only that many people died, with no link to conquest, does not earn the point.

parts.modelAnswer: The account was compiled by a Spanish friar working with Nahua scholars, so it reaches us through Spanish mediation. A student must therefore check its details against other records before treating any single claim as settled fact.
parts.prompt: Explain one limitation of using this account as evidence about the epidemic.

scoring.criterion: Earns the point for explaining one accurate limitation, such as Spanish mediation, the account's focus on one city, or the lack of numbers in the text.
scoring.notEarned: Stating only that the account is old, with no limitation explained, does not earn the point.

source: original; stimulus is a paraphrase of a public-domain primary source

stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of a Nahua account in the Florentine Codex (16th century), public domain; compiled by Bernardino de Sahagun with Nahua scholars.
stimulus.text: Paraphrase of a Nahua account of smallpox in Tenochtitlan, recorded in the Florentine Codex, compiled by the Franciscan friar Bernardino de Sahagun with Nahua scholars in the 1500s. The account describes the sick lying in their houses and sleeping places, no longer able to move or stir, while the healthy could not bury the dead fast enough. Whole neighborhoods fell ill at once.
